intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene on chromosome 22.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: These two variants were inherited from her heterozygous parents, consistent with autosomal recessive genetic transmission.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports compound heterozygous MEI1 mutations causing embryonic arrest in one patient. It never mentions homozygous mutations.

checks.claim: The MEI1 gene is located on chromosome 22.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified two novel pathogenic frameshift variants in the MEI1 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. Standard gene location is accepted as nomenclature restatement.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is an autosomal recessive form of female infertility. Affected women have primary infertility with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure during assisted reproduction (Dong et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2026). Some patients show abnormal fertilization, with tripronuclear or polypronuclear zygotes (Jiao et al., 2025). Embryos from affected women have been found to carry extensive chromosomal abnormalities (Wu et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025; Jiao et al., 2025).

checks.claim: OZEMA26 is an autosomal recessive form of female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Apart from recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
checks.explanation: Biallelic mutations in an autosomal gene causing female infertility imply autosomal recessive inheritance; the term itself is not used in the abstract.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA26 have primary infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Nine primary infertility patients were recruited from the reproduction centers in local hospitals.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA26 have early embryonic arrest during assisted reproduction.

checks.explanation: Early embryonic arrest is stated; patients were recruited from reproduction centers.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA26 have recurrent implantation failure during assisted reproduction.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified several novel mutations in MEI1 causing new phenotypes of early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

checks.claim: Some patients with OZEMA26 show abnormal fertilization with tripronuclear or polypronuclear zygotes.
checks.evidence_quote: the primary characteristic observed in these patients was fertilization resulting in tri-pronuclear (3PN) or poly-pronuclear (PPN) embryos following ICSI

checks.claim: Embryos from women with OZEMA26 have been found to carry extensive chromosomal abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Notably, two Day 3 embryos and two Day 6 blastocysts were all aneuploid, with numerous monosomy and trisomy events.

paragraphs.text: Dong et al. (2021) studied a family in which 2 sisters had recurrent hydatidiform moles. They then screened for MEI1 mutations in patients with embryonic arrest, recurrent implantation failure, and recurrent pregnancy loss, and identified 7 more patients from 6 families. Altogether there were 9 patients with primary infertility from 7 independent families. Besides recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic MEI1 mutations were associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.

paragraphs.text: Jiao et al. (2025) reported 2 unrelated Chinese women with primary infertility and repeated failure of in vitro fertilization (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). The proband in family 1 was 32 years old and had had primary infertility for 4 years. Her menstrual cycles were regular, her ovarian reserve was normal, and she had a normal karyotype. Of 25 oocytes retrieved, 22 were mature. Ten mature oocytes underwent ICSI, and 8 of these formed tripronuclear (3PN) or polypronuclear (PPN) zygotes. Of the 12 oocytes fertilized by conventional IVF, 5 formed normal 2-pronuclear (2PN) zygotes and 3 formed 3PN/PPN zygotes. None of the 2PN-derived embryos reached the blastocyst stage, so no embryos were frozen or transferred. However, 2 of 3 embryos derived from 3PN/PPN zygotes after ICSI developed into late-stage blastocysts. The proband in family 2 was 35 years old and had had primary infertility for 8 years. Her menstrual cycles were regular and her ovarian function was normal. Before her ICSI cycle she had undergone 2 unsuccessful IVF cycles. In the ICSI cycle, 11 oocytes were retrieved; 2PN zygotes formed, and 1 oocyte formed a 1-pronuclear zygote. None of her embryos formed blastocysts. Two frozen embryos were transferred, but she did not become pregnant. In both probands, most day-3 embryos were of high quality at the 7- to 9-cell stage. Jiao et al. (2025) noted that, unlike previously reported MEI1-related phenotypes, the main feature in these patients was the formation of 3PN or PPN zygotes after ICSI.

paragraphs.text: Jiao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in 20 women who had a high rate of abnormal fertilization with ICSI. They identified compound heterozygous MEI1 mutations in 2 unrelated women. The proband in family 1 carried a ser208-to-pro (S208P) missense mutation (c.622T-C) and an arg883-to-ter (R883X) nonsense mutation (c.2647C-T). The proband in family 2 carried a trp1013-to-gly (W1013G) missense mutation (c.3037T-G) and a deletion of exons 21 through 31. The paper gives this deletion as c.2546_3525del in the abstract and results text, and as c.2546_3825del in the figure legend, Table 2, and discussion. Because the deletion covers the c.3037 position, the W1013G mutation appeared homozygous on exome and Sanger sequencing. Quantitative PCR confirmed the copy number loss. All 4 mutations affected highly conserved residues. Under ACMG criteria, R883X was classified as pathogenic, the exon 21-31 deletion as likely pathogenic, and S208P and W1013G as variants of uncertain significance. In transfected HEK293T cells, R883X increased MEI1 mRNA but reduced MEI1 protein, and W1013G increased the protein level. S208P and the exon 21-31 deletion did not change protein expression. MEI1 mRNA levels in peripheral blood from both probands were significantly higher than in controls.

paragraphs.text: Wu et al. (2024) used whole-genome bisulfite sequencing on 2 blastocysts from a woman with compound heterozygous MEI1 mutations. Global methylation levels were 0.344 and 0.168, well outside the optimal range of 0.25 to 0.27. Both blastocysts were also aneuploid. Wu et al. paragraphs.text: Jiao et al. (2025) analyzed 3 embryos from the proband in family 1, who carried the S208P and R883X mutations. Whole-genome sequencing showed chromosomal aneuploidies in a 3PN-derived blastocyst and a 2PN-derived blastomere. Quantitative parental contamination testing and kinship analysis showed that all 3 embryos were triploid, with excess maternal and little paternal genetic material. Haplotype analysis indicated that the triploidy arose in meiosis: in meiosis II in the 3PN zygote, and in meiosis I in the 3PN blastocyst and the 2PN blastomere. RNA sequencing of day-3 embryos found 2,005 downregulated and 1,904 upregulated genes compared with control embryos. Downregulated genes were enriched for meiotic cell cycle functions and epigenetic regulation of transcription, including histone demethylase and deacetylase activity. Several maternal-effect genes were dysregulated, including FBXO43, OOEP, and WEE2. Quantitative PCR confirmed reduced mRNA levels of MEI1, MKI67, ASTL, and WEE2.

paragraphs.text: In a woman with embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure (OZEMA26), Wu et al. (2024) identified a 1-bp deletion (c.3002delC, NM_152513.3) in the MEI1 gene. The deletion causes a frameshift. She was compound heterozygous for this mutation and a 16-bp deletion, c.2264_2268+11delGTGAGGTATGGACCAC. The mutations were found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and each was inherited from a heterozygous parent. Her embryos were aneuploid and had abnormal global DNA methylation levels.

paragraphs.text: In 2 infertile sibs from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) identified a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene. The woman had embryonic arrest (OZEMA26) and the man had azoospermia. The deletion was found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by cDNA sequencing, and the patients had almost no detectable expression of exon 19. Their mother was a heterozygous carrier. On Western blot analysis, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20. The woman's arrested embryos had many chromosomal anomalies.

paragraphs.text: In a 32-year-old Chinese woman with primary infertility, 3PN/PPN zygotes after ICSI, and failure of 2PN-derived embryos to reach the blastocyst stage (OZEMA26), Jiao et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the MEI1 gene. One was a c.622T-C transition causing a ser208-to-pro (S208P) substitution, and the other was a c.2647C-T transition causing an arg883-to-ter (R883X) substitution. The mutations were found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. S208P affected a conserved residue and was classified as a variant of uncertain significance. It did not change protein expression in transfected HEK293T cells. R883X reduced MEI1 protein in HEK293T cells and was classified as pathogenic. Embryos from the patient were triploid, with excess maternal genetic material, and some were aneuploid.

paragraphs.text: In a 35-year-old Chinese woman with 8 years of primary infertility (OZEMA26), Jiao et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the MEI1 gene. None of her embryos formed blastocysts, and transfer of frozen embryos did not lead to pregnancy. One mutation was a c.3037T-G transversion causing a trp1013-to-gly (W1013G) substitution. The other was a deletion of exons 21 through 31, given as c.2546_3525del in the abstract and results text and as c.2546_3825del in Table 2 and the discussion. Because the deletion covers c.3037, W1013G appeared homozygous on sequencing, and quantitative PCR confirmed the copy number loss. W1013G affected a conserved residue, increased MEI1 protein levels in transfected HEK293T cells, and was classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The exon 21-31 deletion did not change protein expression and was classified as likely pathogenic.
